misconceptions.description: Treating every kind of cognitive load as something to minimize, including the germane processing that builds schemas.
misconceptions.trigger: learner proposes cutting self-explanation, practice, or elaboration to reduce load
misconceptions.feedback: Distinguish the three loads. Cut extraneous load, manage intrinsic load, but protect and support germane load, the processing that builds the schema.

misconceptions.description: Believing intrinsic load is a fixed property of the material that is identical for every learner, ignoring that element interactivity is relative to existing schemas.
misconceptions.trigger: diagnosis names high intrinsic load without naming the target learner's prior knowledge
misconceptions.feedback: Intrinsic load depends on element interactivity relative to the learner. State who the learner is; an expert's schemas chunk elements and lower the load.

misconceptions.description: Assuming the only way to lower intrinsic load is to delete essential content, rather than sequencing or pre-training.
misconceptions.trigger: learner proposes removing essential steps to make a complex task easier
misconceptions.feedback: Manage intrinsic load with pre-training, segmenting, and sequencing so fewer novel elements interact at once, without deleting essential content.
